(Baton Rouge, Louisiana) | college = [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] (2013–2015) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2015) * SEC All-Freshman team (2014) * [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]] (2013) * First-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2013) }} '''Jarell Martin''' (born May 24, 1994) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently closed his college career at [[Louisiana State University]]. Mickey, a 6'10" [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] from [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]], is considered one of the top players in college basketball and a likely first-round pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].{{cite web | last = Mickles | first = Sheldon | title = LSU forwards Mickey, Martin projected as second-round picks | work = [[Baton Rouge Advocate]] | date = January 14, 2015 | url = http://theadvocate.com/sports/lsu/11532363-123/lsus-jordan-mickey-jarell-martin | accessdate = March 10, 2015}} ==High school career== [[File:20130403 MCDAAG Jarell Martin tomahawk dunk (1).JPG|Martin in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]|thumb|left|upright]] As one of the top prospects in the country, Martin was selected as a [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]], the first for LSU head coach [[Johnny Jones (basketball, born 1961)|Johnny Jones]]. Martin was also the winner of the 2013 [[Louisiana Mr. Basketball|Mr. Basketball award]] given annually by the Louisiana Sports Writers Association to the top player in the state of Louisiana. Considered a five-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Martin was listed as the No. 3 power forward and the No. 11 player in the nation in 2013.[http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/138383/jarrell-martin Jarell Martin Recruiting Profile] ==College career== ===Freshman Season=== Started 25 of LSU’s 34 games, averaging 10.3 points, 4.6 rebounds and 26.2 minutes per contest. He ranked ninth in the SEC among freshmen in scoring, seventh among SEC frosh in rebounding. He averaged 11.4 points per game in SEC action with 12 of his 18 double figure scoring games coming in SEC play.
